newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot power climbs on cooler forecast.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot power climbs on cooler forecast.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly higher Monday, climbing on forecasts of below normal temperatures and under some influence from strong natural gas prices, sources said.
Below normal temperatures with scattered heavy snow flurries were expected to move through much of the Mid-West this week, boosting power demand and spot prices, brokers and marketers said.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were discussed mostly in the $21.00-22.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, compared with Friday's trading range of $16.00-17.50.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power for Tuesday was said to be holding steady in the $11.00-12.00 range, the sources said.
Enron Corp said a natural gas compressor station on its Northern Border pipeline had been restored to service Monday afternoon after being shut over the weekend for a valve repair.
The closure of the station near Aberdeen, S.D. did not impact about 1.7 billion cubic feet per day of deliveries on the Northern Border system.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday climbed into the $20.00-22.00 range from Friday's trading range of $19.00-21.50, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power for Tuesday was assessed higher at $13.00-15.00 from $11.00-12.00 late last week, the sources said.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday were talked in the $20.00-22.00 range, as compared with Friday's $16.00-17.00 trading range, the sources said.
ECAR peak prices were reported to have moved even higher into the $26.00-27.00 range in morning trade, but backed off in the afternoon, the sources said.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were quoted higher at $14.00-16.00 from $11.00-$12.00 late last week.
February ECAR was assessed little changed in the $23.00-24.00 range.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), where temperatures were expected to fall to well below-normal by week's end, peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery climbed into the $19.00-22.00 range from Friday's $15.00-16.00 trading range.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP for Tuesday delivery were notionally assessed higher at $12.00-13.00 from $11.00-12.00 on Friday.
Balance of January peak prices in SPP were said to have moved up to the $22.50-24.00 range from $20.00-22.00 last week, while February SPP was set at $25.50-26.25, the sources said.
Separately, Detroit Edison's 1,116 megawatt (MW) Fermi 2 nuclear unit in Michigan was operating at 50 percent power early Monday morning.
Also, American Electric Power Co's 1,090 MW Cook 2 nuclear unit in Michigan, which had been operating at 55 percent power, has returned to full power.
Furthermore, Commonwealth Edison's 794 MW Dresden 2 unit in Illinois continued to increase power and was at 87 percent of capacity as of early this morning.
Consumers Energy's 780 MW Palisades nuclear unit in Michigan, shut Sunday for electrical repairs, will likely resume service later today.
Duquesne Light Co said the restart of its 833 MW Beaver Valley 2 unit in Pennsylvania, shut early Monday, is not yet known.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
